### Generation of New Organelles and Cell Function

*   The cell's ability to generate new organelles and control its general function is crucial for its survival and proper functioning. This process is controlled by three checkpoints that are built into cell division.

### Three Checkpoints in Cell Division

*   In eukaryotic cells, these checkpoints are points within cell division where the cell can go one of three ways:
    *   Cell division can be halted temporarily or permanently
    *   Cell division can proceed
    *   Cell death can be triggered
*   These checkpoints have been evolutionarily conserved, meaning that the mechanisms in fruit flies are very similar to those in our own bodies.

### The Role of Checkpoints in Cell Division

*   At each of the three checkpoints, the cell determines whether or not all of the components and conditions have been met for cell division to proceed.
*   Each checkpoint involves numerous molecules interacting in a set of complex cell signaling pathways.
*   A change to these signaling pathways can cause cell division by promoting molecules to be expressed more than usual or by hindering molecules expression.
*   Any of these changes in a normal cell's signaling pathways can cause the cell to replicate out of control—this is cancer.
